G3017G.name: Levi
G3017G.desc: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
G3017G.brief: Son of Melchi, an ancestor of Jesus
G3017G.short: Levi, son of Melchi, an ancestor of Jesus mentioned in Luke's genealogy (<ref="Luk.3.24">Luk.3.24</ref>).

G3017H.name: Levi
G3017H.desc: Man living at the time of Divided Monarchy
G3017H.brief: Son of Simeon, an ancestor of Jesus
G3017H.short: Levi, son of Simeon, an ancestor of Jesus mentioned in Luke's genealogy (<ref="Luk.3.29">Luk.3.29</ref>).

G3044.name: Linus
G3044.desc: Man living at the time of the New Testament
G3044.brief: Christian in Rome; greeted by Paul
G3044.short: Linus, a Christian in Rome to whom Paul sent greetings.

G3090.name: Lois
G3090.desc: Woman living at the time of the New Testament
G3090.brief: Grandmother of Timothy; commended for her faith
G3090.short: Lois, the grandmother of Timothy, was commended by Paul for her sincere faith.

G3066.name: Lucius
G3066.desc: Man living at the time of the New Testament
G3066.brief: Prophet and teacher in the church at Antioch.
G3066.short: Lucius of Cyrene was a prophet and teacher in the church at Antioch who was involved in sending Paul and Barnabas on their first missionary journey.

G3065.name: Luke
G3065.desc: Man living at the time of the New Testament
G3065.brief: Physician; companion of Paul; author of Luke and Acts
G3065.short: Luke, a physician and companion of Paul, was the author of the Gospel of Luke and the Book of Acts.

G3070.name: Lydia
G3070.desc: Woman living at the time of the New Testament
G3070.brief: Seller of purple goods; converted by Paul in Philippi
G3070.short: Lydia, a seller of purple goods from Thyatira, was converted by Paul in Philippi and hosted the church in her home.

G3078.name: Lysanias
G3078.desc: Tetrarch of Abilene living at the time of the New Testament
G3078.brief: Tetrarch of Abilene during John the Baptist's ministry
G3078.short: Lysanias, the tetrarch of Abilene, ruled during the time of John the Baptist's ministry (<ref="Luk.3.1">Luk.3.1</ref>).

G3079.name: Lysias
G3079.desc: Man living at the time of the New Testament
G3079.brief: Roman commander who rescued Paul from a Jewish mob
G3079.short: Claudius Lysias, the Roman commander in Jerusalem, rescued Paul from a Jewish mob and sent him to Felix.

G3092.name: Maath
G3092.desc: Man living at the time of Exile and Return
G3092.short: Maath is mentioned in the genealogy of Jesus Christ as recorded in the Gospel of Luke.

G3071.name: Lycaonia
G3071.brief: A region in Asia Minor; Paul and Barnabas preached there
G3071.short: Lycaonia, a region in Asia Minor where Paul and Barnabas preached the gospel (<ref="Act.14.6, 11">Act.14.6, 11</ref>).

G3073.name: Lycia
G3073.brief: A region on the southwest coast of Asia Minor
G3073.short: Lycia, a region on the southwest coast of Asia Minor, passed by Paul on his journey to Rome (<ref="Act.27.5">Act.27.5</ref>).

G3082.name: Lystra
G3082.brief: A city in Lycaonia; Paul and Barnabas preached there
G3082.short: Lystra, a city in Lycaonia where Paul and Barnabas preached and Paul healed a lame man (<ref="Act.14.6-21">Act.14.6-21</ref>).

G3093.name: Magadan
G3093.brief: A place on the Sea of Galilee; home of Mary Magdalene
G3093.short: Magadan (Dalmanutha), a place on the shore of the Sea of Galilee visited by Jesus (<ref="Matthew 15:39; Mrk.8.10">Matthew 15:39; Mrk.8.10</ref>), possibly the hometown of Mary Magdalene (<ref="Matthew 27:56, 61; 28:1; Mrk.15.40, 47; 16:1, 9; Luke 8:2; 24:10; Jhn.19.25; 20:1, 18">Matthew 27:56, 61; 28:1; Mrk.15.40, 47; 16:1, 9; Luke 8:2; 24:10; Jhn.19.25; 20:1, 18</ref>).

G3032.name: Freedmen
G3032.brief: Former slaves who had been granted freedom
G3032.short: The Freedmen, mentioned in <ref="Act.6.9">Act.6.9</ref>, were likely former Jewish slaves who had been granted freedom and had their own synagogue in Jerusalem.

G3003.name: Legion
G3003.brief: Name of a demon or group of demons
G3003.short: In the New Testament, Legion is the name given to a demon or group of demons that possessed a man in the region of the Gerasenes (<ref="Mrk.5.9; Luke 8:30">Mrk.5.9; Luke 8:30</ref>).
